readiness.guidance: Training volume and intensity must be held at minimum viable levels until objective recovery metrics (especially HRV and sleep) are restored and reported.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a dramatic drop in volume and frequency, with modest pace improvement but declining efficiency — consistent with deconditioning or forced reduction due to fatigue or external stress.
monthly_review.highlight: The 69.2 km drop in monthly volume — from 78.5 km to just 9.3 km — is not a blip but a full-order-of-magnitude reduction, confirmed across all prior months (June–September consistently >51 km), indicating a hard break in training continuity rather than normal variation.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month would require 69.2 km across 13 sessions (~5.3 km/session) in 29 days — but given compromised readiness and absence of recovery metrics, chasing this volume is unsafe and counterproductive; priority must shift to restoring baseline readiness before rebuilding load.

insights.title: Pace improved despite higher HR and worse efficiency
insights.body: Avg pace quickened by 30 sec/km while avg HR rose (+2 bpm) and running economy worsened (+0.35 ml/kg/km) — suggesting compensation via less efficient mechanics or elevated sympathetic tone rather than true aerobic gain.

insights.title: Cadence surge without stride length increase
insights.body: Cadence jumped +8 spm (146 → 154) while recent stride length (80–86 cm) remains stable and below July’s peak (86.49 cm on 2026-09-24), implying shorter, choppier steps — often seen with fatigue or reduced leg spring efficiency.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance persists amid volume crash
insights.body: Zone 3 still accounts for 31% of effort this month (vs 33% in Sept, 29% in July), even as total volume collapsed — indicating disproportionate reliance on moderate-intensity work without sufficient Z1/Z2 base or Z4/Z5 stimulus, likely impairing recovery capacity.

insights.title: Longest run shrank from 14.8 km (July) to 4.8 km (Oct)
insights.body: The longest run decreased by 10.0 km over three months (14.8 → 12.0 → 10.7 → 4.8), tracking precisely with the progressive decline in weekly volume and aerobic TE — a red flag for endurance reserve erosion.

recommendations.action: Complete 3x Zone 1 runs (HR ≤128 bpm) of 35–45 min each, no distance target — stop if HR drifts >5 bpm above baseline or cadence drops >5 spm
recommendations.reason: Zone 1 preserves aerobic base while minimizing autonomic stress; HR ceiling set 10 bpm below lowest recent avg HR (134 in Aug) to accommodate current compromised status

recommendations.action: Perform daily 5-min HRV-guided breathing (inhale 5s, exhale 6s) and log sleep duration — no running if <6.5 hrs slept the prior night
recommendations.reason: Directly addresses missing recovery signals by building parasympathetic capacity and enforcing sleep-based gatekeeping

recommendations.action: Replace one scheduled run with 20 min barefoot calf + glute activation drills on grass (3x10 heel raises, 3x12 single-leg bridges, 3x30 sec single-leg balance eyes closed)
recommendations.reason: Counters deteriorating stride integrity and ground contact time stability (300–318 ms range) with neuromuscular reconnection

risk_flags.evidence: Longest run dropped 10.0 km since July; avg efficiency worsened 0.47 ml/kg/km from June (13.46) to now (14.93); aerobic TE increased 0.4 pts from June (2.7) to now (3.0)
risk_flags.action: Prioritise 3+ Z1 sessions weekly and delay any zone 3+ efforts until efficiency stabilises ≤14.6 and longest run ≥8 km

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence up +8 spm but stride length unchanged and vertical oscillation holding at 8.1–8.6 cm (above ideal ≤7.5 cm for recreational runners), suggesting compensatory stiffness or reduced elastic return
risk_flags.action: Add daily mobility + barefoot activation as prescribed; monitor vertical oscillation — if >8.5 cm persists beyond 10 days, add gait retraining cues

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic control, neuromuscular coordination, and aerobic rhythm — not volume or pace — using heart rate gates, breathwork, and ground-feel drills to rebuild the foundation for sustainable progress.
